comparison: Perfect alignment with 100% claim overlap (C82-C97, C129, C138, C141). Both evaluations support that Hsp110 remodels aggregates to increase Hsp70 binding sites, using microscopy, DLS, and sequential addition experiments. Both rate this as SUPPORTED with strong evidence.

Strong alignment with 77.8% claim overlap (C8, C116-C120, C131). Both evaluations support the novel finding that Hsp110 disrupts JDP-Hsp70 binding through competition. OpenEval emphasizes BLI experiments; peer reviewers highlight this as explaining inhibition at high NEF concentrations. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong alignment with 66.7% claim overlap on mechanistic model claims (C9, C75, C139-C140, C153-C155, C162, C164-C165). Both evaluations agree the proposed mechanism is speculative and rate as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes lack of structural validation; peer reviewers state mechanistic understanding remains incomplete and requires further analysis.

Moderate alignment with 41.9% claim overlap. Both support that class B JDPs show stronger Hsp110 stimulation and increased Hsp70 recruitment (C3-C5, C46-C47, C57-C58, C63-C66, C126-C127). OpenEval includes additional claims about EEVD interaction and human orthologs not explicitly covered in peer result. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap (27.6% claims: C57-C58, C71-C74, C135-C136). Both address Hsp110-dependent increases in Hsp70 binding with class B JDPs. OpenEval R2 focuses on binding kinetics and saturation experiments; Peer R1 emphasizes this as a key finding about aggregate remodeling. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Moderate overlap (55.6% claims: C55-C56, C102-C103, C128). Both support stage-specific effects of Hsp110 (stimulation in disaggregation, inhibition in folding). OpenEval emphasizes direct comparison experiments; peer reviewers highlight this as placing Hsp110 early in disaggregation. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Good alignment (60% overlap: C121-C123). Both support interdependent effects of Sis1 and Sse1 concentrations demonstrating competition. OpenEval provides quantitative details about inflection points; peer reviewers note stoichiometry as important parameter. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap (30.8% claims: C77-C80). Both support comparative NEF experiments showing Fes1 requires higher concentrations than Sse1. OpenEval provides detailed affinity correlations and cellular abundance context; peer reviewers accept this as part of systematic analysis. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap (27.8% claims: C99-C101, C106-C107). Both address biphasic dose-response and stoichiometry effects. OpenEval R5 focuses on Sse1-2 variant experiments; Peer R4 emphasizes stoichiometry as tuning parameter across systems. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap (27.8% claims: C110-C114). Both address biphasic effects and systematic titration. OpenEval R5 emphasizes dose-response curves with Sse1-2 variant; Peer R7 focuses on comparative NEF experiments. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap (28.6% claims: C145-C148). Both support that human systems tolerate higher Hsp110 levels than yeast, and class B JDPs tolerate higher levels than class A. OpenEval includes stage-specific effects; peer reviewers focus on stoichiometry tuning. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Minor overlap (12% claims: C68-C70). Both support EEVD interaction requirement through mutant experiments. OpenEval R1 includes this as part of broader class B JDP findings; Peer R6 specifically highlights structural requirements. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Minor overlap (11.8% claims: C59-C60). Both address use of multiple substrates (luciferase, GFP). OpenEval R2 emphasizes substrate consistency in binding experiments; Peer R8 highlights multiple substrates as methodological strength for general conclusions. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Minor overlap (10.5% claims: C61-C62). Both address ATP-dependence controls. OpenEval R2 includes this in broader binding kinetics analysis; Peer R11 treats as standard control experiments. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Minor overlap (9.5% claims: C89, C95). Both address ATP-dependence in aggregate remodeling experiments. OpenEval R3 includes this in comprehensive remodeling analysis; Peer R11 treats as control experiments establishing specificity. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

OpenEval R10 addresses evolutionary speculation about cellular abundance correspondence and human system adaptation (C143-C144, C150). No corresponding peer review evaluation found. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are hypothetical interpretations without experimental testing.

Peer R6 addresses EEVD interaction requirement and structural requirements (C68-C70, C134) as a distinct supported finding. While OpenEval R1 includes some overlapping claims (C68-C70), Peer R6 treats this as a separate mechanistic finding about structural requirements for Sse1-Sis1 cooperation.

Peer R8 specifically highlights use of multiple substrates (C59-C60) as a methodological strength enabling general conclusions. While OpenEval R2 includes these claims, peer reviewers treat the multi-substrate approach as a distinct strength of the systematic analysis.

Peer R11 addresses ATP-dependence and specificity controls (C61-C62, C89, C95) as a distinct set of supporting experiments. While OpenEval R2 and R3 include these claims, peer reviewers group these as standard control experiments establishing active chaperone function.
